A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fiber-coupling study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original laboratory training, coupling-speed and misalignment experiments, motor characterization, and virtual-testbed studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds CrossQ experiments and further SAC comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds CrossQ as an alternative learning component for direct experimental training alongside SAC and TQC. The four-dimensional actions, history-based observations, reward function, reset procedure, and curriculum mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same physical fiber-coupling apparatus and Gaussian virtual testbed, including manual misalignment, shifted coupling maxima, and action-noise scenarios. The additional learners operate within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: CrossQ joins the laboratory comparisons in Figure 2 and the six existing virtual-testbed algorithms in Figure 11. SAC also newly participates in the P_goal = 0.9 laboratory comparison and post-training coupling tests, previously restricted to TQC variants and the human comparator where applicable.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises the stated main-experiment goal-power range from [0.8, 0.9] to [0.85, 0.9]. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. The 30-step episode limit and 100 RL versus 25 human test repetitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 3 removes failure-probability evidence from the manual-versus-automatic reset robustness comparison. Otherwise, the reward, episode-length, reset, curriculum, observation, drift, action-size, noise, replay-buffer, and simulation-pre-training analyses in Appendices C–D are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use smoothed means with 2σ bands, retain the power-measurement uncertainty, and report the same repeated-run conventions. These conventions extend to the added learners; no new seed disclosure, confidence-interval method, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 11 add substantial algorithm results. At P_goal = 0.9, v3 reports approximately 120,000 training steps for SAC/CrossQ versus 200,000 for TQC, and CrossQ needs at most seven steps in 75% of final successful episodes. CrossQ replaces SAC as the preferred virtual-testbed algorithm, especially at the highest goal. Table 3 removes both p[fail] = 0.03 entries; its remaining numerical differences are rounding.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, observation and reward definitions, Gaussian testbed equation, and noise-model reasoning are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central claim of model-free, in-situ learning achieving 90% coupling remains. v3 adds the headline claim that CrossQ couples faster and requires roughly half TQC's training time. The abstract also clarifies that training avoids simulation pre-training.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds an argument about transferring simulator findings to the laboratory, distinguishing idealized independent actions from noisy, coupled physical actuation. Section 5 qualifies the curriculum-learning conclusion as helpful for TQC but unnecessary for CrossQ, and removes v2's hypothesis connecting occasional slow coupling to dependence between episodes.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds CrossQ settings, including learning rate 0.0003, replay-buffer size 1,000,000, batch size 256, and discount factor 0.99. Existing learner settings, apparatus details, GPU information, and code-access disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bhatt et al. on CrossQ, Singh et al.'s robotics survey, and Golemo et al. on simulation-to-reality transfer. A new related-work paragraph positions actuator backlash against the more commonly discussed problem of noisy observations. The existing optics positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The principal sections and appendix organization remain. There are targeted abstract, results, and outlook rewrites, added explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgment edits, and conversion from numbered to author–date citations; most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout into the TMLR style. Figure 2 becomes a full-page display with rearranged panels, expanded comparisons, and revised colors, legends, and axes. Figure 11 gains CrossQ curves, Table 3 loses a column, and Figures 13–14 move after Appendix E.

improvement.justification: v2 selected TQC for subsequent laboratory experiments largely from its lower-goal performance. v3 directly compares alternatives at the difficult 0.9 goal and qualifies the curriculum conclusion, providing better support for algorithm selection. The gains are bounded: uncertainty practices remain unchanged, Table 3 loses failure information, and the new claim of always beating the human is stronger than the overlapping time distributions alone establish.
